quest.title: The Lone Phantom Sail
quest.description: Ahes seems to be looking for you...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x300, Primogem x40, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3, Strange Part x1

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Hello, I'm Ahes. It's a pleasure to meet a new friend!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi, Ahes! Paimon's Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #Hello there, I'm {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Verenata told me that you found "that ship" too! Is it true? Is it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Well, there are a lot of ships in the ocean, but...

choices.text: Which ship do you speak of?

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Th—That very unique ship!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oooh... that ship, huh...

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Haha! Sorry, forgive me! I must have confused you!

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Ahem, the ship I mentioned is the Sponsian, a white ironclad ship that sails through dreams, and the explorer of whirlpools and the abyss... It's the flagship of Admiral Basil Elton!

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Captain Basil left a faded shipwreck and a tattered logbook in these waters... I come here every day to pick up and read everything with writing on them!

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Hehe, so you can consider me a Sponsian archaeologist! I know everything about her! Well, not everything-everything, but I know at least half of her!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! You must really love this ship, huh? You just can't stop talking about her once you start.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But since even you only know half... She must've been a huge ship, then!

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Well... She isn't that huge... because Captain Basil only left half of its hull behind...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, so...

choices.text: So, you came to us.

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Haha, yeah! I knew you would understand!

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Verenata told me! She said that you saw her in an illusion — the Sponsian, she who sails forward eternally! She who's returned from the paradise of Cathuria!

choices.text: Her front half, to be precise...

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Indeed! Her front half! The unsinkable front half! I knew she was still discovering new waters! Still fighting desperately against the reefs, the whirlpools, and the dark fleets! Still, she...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! Calm down! Um... You still haven't told us what you need help with.

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: #Huh? Help? Oh... I don't plan on asking for your help, not really. But since you've seen the Sponsian, {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Well... I'm looking for it, so why don't you come along?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Heh, your enthusiasm's making it hard to say no... And you mentioned a shipwreck... Where there's a wreck, there's a treasure... so yeah, we can join you!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's go meet this lady of the sea.

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Yes, that's the spirit! Let's set sail!

choices.text: I'm not certain that was her, exactly, but we did see half a transparent ship...

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: I'm certain! That must've been her! I've never once faltered — I've always known, ever since she responded to me! I knew she wasn't gone!

choices.text: So that's what you mean by "that ship"...
Oh! That ship!

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Yes, yes, that one!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that one! Paimon thought you were talking about a different one! Haha...

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Then... which ship were you thinking about?

choices.text: Uh... Well... The one you mentioned?

talks.objective: Go to the place Ahes mentioned

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: This is the place! We've arrived!

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Um, please wait just a moment... Allow me to tune the conch a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? "Tune"... a conch? Is that a part of the grilling process...?

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Oh, come on. All you know is eat, eat, eat! This is a military conch for communication!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A... military conch?

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Yes, this is an old military conch. Ancient sailors used conches as a tool to communicate with each other... It must be a relic left behind from when the navy still existed. I found it in a sunken wreck.

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: When I tuned the conch here last time, I heard her response. Since you've seen her, I think you should be able to hear her response too!

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: But you'll have to wait a moment, you know! I have to tune the conch before I can send out the proper signal.

choices.text: In other words, that ship can receive a specific signal.

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Yes, that's correct. However, both the time of day and the conditions of the sea will affect the conch's signal generation, so you have to constantly tune it to make sure it'll work. Hehe... that's the problem with antiques.

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Hmm, anyway, please wait while I tune this conch to align with the vibration of the waves. Don't go running too far away now!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Ahes deftly works with the conch in her hand, and not long after, the tuning is complete...

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Okay, that's it! Hehe, I've learned a lot from those ancient seafarer manuals!

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Now, allow me to give you a little primer. There are three kinds of short signals that I usually use...

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: "Long low note, short low note, long low note." Yes... This one should mean... Well, my guess is that it probably means "Ready and waiting."

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: "Long low note, long low note, long low note, long low note, long low note." This one means... Um, I'm not actually sure, but the response I received last time was something like that, so it's definitely useful for something!

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: "Short low note, long low note, short low note, long low note, short low note, long low note, short low note, long low note, short low note, long low note"... Phew! This is a long one, for sure! This is the signal that has the highest likelihood of receiving a response, and as for its meaning...

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: According to the manual at least... it means "I have a message to send."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... So, what should we do to figure out the signal that will receive a response?

choices.text: Use deduction to find the corresponding signal?

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Yuck, no way. That's far too random, and we have too little concrete information... It's true that I've received some mysterious responses back after sending out these three signals, but...

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: But I've yet to discover any logical relationship between the signals and the appearance of the Sponsian...

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: So, all we can do is to try them all, one at a time...

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: So, which one should we start with?

choices.text: Let's try the signals one at a time?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Can't we use some sort of time-saving method... or something a bit smarter? Like... deduction or something!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You try, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe... If Paimon was to start using deductive reasoning, then why don't we make a chart and find the signal with the highest response rate? That should be the signal we're looking for!

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: ...Hmm, though we are in Fontaine, and most ships are required to respond to signals by law... the ship we're looking for isn't normal in any sense of the word, you know?

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: So, we can't expect her to consistently respond to the same signals... In other words, the fundamental requirements for deductive reasoning to work simply don't apply here. Too many things are random, and we lack any evidence to work off of.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Urgh... Th—Then let's just try them one at a time...

choices.text: So are you saying... that she will appear when you send the signal?

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Hehe, pretty cool, isn't it? She's just like a whale! You sing, and she responds. I've heard the sound with my own ears, it's true.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's start from the longest one.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's start from the shortest one.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's start with the one of middling length.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm not sure. What would you prefer, Ahes?

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Ah, me? Um... if you're asking me, then I would pick this one.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Ahes sends the signal with the conch...

talks.objective: Use the conches to send the signal

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: What happened here... It's a complete mess. There isn't even a complete wreck, it's mostly just... fragments.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Signs point to her being still further up ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: But she must have suffered irreparable damage, so why would she still forge onward in such poor condition? Unless... Hmm. I think we'll find out why soon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So many tiny little pieces everywhere! It's like she was *chomp* bitten in half by a giant sea monster!

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Eh... Did you hear it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What...

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Shh, the signal... Wait... Her! It's her, she's over there! In the distance!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Paimon... Paimon can't see anything!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I saw it.

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Yes! I knew you'd able to see it too! Quick, after her, let's catch up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Catch... catch what? The ship? Have you two grown sails and sprouted oars or something!?

talks.objective: Follow the phantom that has appeared
Follow the phantom that has appeared

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Which is to say, the Sponsian suffered heavy damage, and the damage was related to the abyss expedition, and... she continued to sail on. In that case...

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Let's use the conch to send out another signal! Maybe we'll hear her response from up ahead!

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Oh right, right! The signals you want to send are "long low note, short low note, long low note"...

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: "Long low note, long low note, long low note, long low note, long low note," and... Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: "Short low note, long low note, short low note, long low note, short low note, long low note, short low note, long low note, short low note, long low note"... Gah, this one is super lengthy! But these three signals should all get you a response!

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Strange... Why won't she show herself?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gah... Even though Paimon can't see that ship, so far, she's still been following you two around on this wild goose chase...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But since it disappeared here, perhaps it's a hint to tell us to find something? For all you know, there might be lost treasure here!

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Hehe, little jellyfish Paimon sure is greedy.

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: But what we're looking for isn't treasure at all... Yes, if we have to give it a name, isn't it closer to "proof"?

choices.text: By "proof," you mean...?

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Proof that the Sponsian passed through this place. Such as a navigation log, any wreckage from the boat itself, or nautical tools... Anyway, we should be able to find something related to her!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... so no treasure then...

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: We can use the conch to send out sounds, and analyze the returning sound waves to determine the ship's approximate location.

choices.text: Don't despair, Paimon. There might be treasure too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! That's just what Paimon thinks!

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Perhaps... But we're not here to find sunken treasure this time. What we want is proof that the "Sponsian" passed this way.

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Navigation logs, wreckage from the boat itself, or nautical tools... Anyway, we should be able to find something related to her!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... It's a box and a... bucket? Maybe we should open them up and take a look? They just might be...

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Rocks. They are rocks.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! Really valuable rocks!

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Hahaha, silly Paimon! They're ballast! Ballast used to stabilize the weight of the battleship!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Oh... then... Paimon guesses that there's no such thing as valuable ballast then...

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: But since we found so much ballast dumped in a single location, perhaps the ship had to execute an emergency maneuver to increase buoyancy...

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: In other words, she must have been forced to take extreme measures to evade danger, despite being the flagship of the ironclad armada...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Busted wooden planks, oars, and... the wreck of a small boat. There's nothing worth looking at here...

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: It's a lifeboat... So even the lifeboats were destroyed? ...Oh? Look over there. What's that between the boards?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmmm... It looks like a scrap of paper... Is it the log? Should we take it out and have a look?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They came here to fight against monsters from the Abyss...

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Yes... I have heard of legends regarding them before. But... does that mean that the Sponsian has already...

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Hmph! This isn't enough proof. Let's go to the next location.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's start from the shortest one.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I choose the longest one.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's start with the one of middling length.

talks.objective: Use the conches to send the signal again

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You told Paimon to hide, and then you went wild on those slimes... Then you picked up a handful of sand and started talking to yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened to you just now? You scared Paimon half to death!

choices.text: I witnessed the moments before the ship sank...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Wait... So you thought you were fighting a group of monsters from the Abyss? No wonder you had that scarily serious look on your face!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph. If you ask Paimon, this is all Verenata's potions' fault!

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: What's with all that noise! What are you doing!? Were you trying to haul the wreck off while I wasn't around?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Is the wood from shipwrecks like these worth a lot?

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: I don't know... Hey, is that really what you're planning!? You... naughty jellyfish!

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Hmm... Even though it's in pieces... Well, bits of it can still be collected as souvenirs...

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: I'm afraid it's probably impossible to restore its original white ironclad appearance... But I can still explore her past experiences... Maybe...

choices.text: Captain Basil seems to have been really fond of you.

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: E—Eh? What...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #It's nothing! {NICKNAME} has been acting strange ever since just now... Maybe some rest will do the trick!

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: #Hahahaha! Don't say that, Paimon! I believe {NICKNAME} saw something we didn't. Well... at the very least, there's no harm in thinking this way.

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Just like... how I believe Captain Basil has always been supporting me...

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: I will find a way to gradually restore her logbook and nautical chart so that her adventures and stories can be marked accurately on our maps!

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: That's what I want to do. Although... the meaning of some names may be lost, and the location of some ports may be known to no one...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That doesn't matter! We can just leave it to people who come after to rediscover them!

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Yes! Thank you for helping me locate the Sponsian! Please accept this gift of mine!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, okay! See you!

choices.text: I heard Captain Basil's voice.
I picked up this silver pendant.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A pendant? But there's nothing in your hands but sand! Huh? Wait, there's also a really small conch...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so you were talking to this "imaginary pendant"? ... That's just the contents of the logbook earlier confusing you, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? This is a... navigation log? It looks like it's relatively intact! Should we give it a read?

talks.objective: Get to the location where the phantom stopped

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, look! This wreckage must've once been the ship we were chasing earlier — or, well, half of it anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Sh—She's all torn up...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey... Don't be so sad, Ahes... We couldn't have expected things to turn out like this, right?

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: I know, but... Oh, forget it... I'll go look around and see if there's anything worth investigating...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yeah, there might be some good stuff left... C'mon, {NICKNAME}, let's have a look around as well!

talks.objective: Look for clues near the wreck

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In other words, this ship must've sunk during the struggle against the sea monster...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then this half was torn up by the waves and floated on the ocean currents before finally settling here.

choices.text: And if it was indeed destroyed by the monster...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, but wouldn't that mean that she really was bitten in half? ... Huh? What's that noise?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, more monsters! Here they come again!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon, hide!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... but... Okay!

choices.text: ...Then her other half might still be inside its body.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
"...Oh leave her, sailors, leave her..."
"...Tomorrow you'll get your pay, and it's time for us to leave her..."
"...Oh leave her, sailors, leave her..."
"For the voyage is done and the winds don't blow, so it's time for us to leave her..."

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "...No grog allowed and rotten grub, and it's time for us to leave her..."\n"...Oh leave her, sailors, leave her..."\n"...The sails all furled, our work is done, and it's time for us to leave her..."

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As the dream-like shanty dissolves into the ocean waves, a sorrowful voice comes from the strange pendant...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "Blue, like a little sailor... I saw her... Haha..."\n"She had the scent of sea monsters on her..."\n"But she is a good child. Perhaps she will not get my flagship dirty..."

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "Heh, it's a shame I couldn't protect her well enough. She was a good boat..."

talks.objective: Talk to Paimon and the others

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: What's wrong, did you forget? The signals you want to send are: "Low, high, low"...

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: "Low, low, low, low, low" and... um...

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: "High, low, high, low, high, low, high, low, high, low"... Phew, that's long! But these three signals should all get you a response!

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Oh, did you forget the signal? It's "long low note, short low note, long low note."

choices.text: Alright, got it!

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Hehe, you've got this!

choices.text: Conches really are tough to operate...

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Well, in that case... Hehe, maybe I should do it myself, then!

choices.text: Don't worry. I'll give this another go.

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: Thank you!

choices.text: Alright, we're counting on you.

response.speaker: Ahes
response.text: I'll take it from here, then!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Ahes sends the signal with the conch...

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Do you still remember the signal? It goes "Short low note, long low note, short low note, long low note, short low note, long low note, short low note, long low note, short low note, long low note"!

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Hehe, it's pretty long, huh?

choices.text: Alright, got it!

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: "Long low note, long low note, long low note, long low note, long low note" — that's how this signal's supposed to go.

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Hmm. Here, aaand... here. They should be marked out on your sea chart now... Anyway, these are my best bets based on the echoes.

dialogues.speaker: Ahes
dialogues.text: Let's investigate these areas next!
